subject: Cross-team: retention scope and BYO-KMS check-in
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@acme.com>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@acme.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Cross-team: retention scope and BYO-KMS check-in

Hi all,

Acme sent over a targeted request this morning and asked that we triage feasibility and owner alignment before EOD Friday. Short version: they need a short-lived exception for a subset of audit logs and a controlled BYO-KMS rotation window tied to a pilot. Key asks from Acme: 1) retention carveout for 'ingest-debug' audit logs for 60 days instead of standard 365; 2) allow a customer-managed key for that dataset with a 48-hour rotation window during the pilot; 3) minimal SSO evidence for auditors (SSO metadata + last 6 months of admin change logs).

Attachments: acme_retention_matrix.xlsx (matrix with the log types they flagged); kms_diagram.png (their proposed key flow).

Can the infra/security/product teams confirm:
- Is a 60-day scoped exception technically possible without changing the global retention service?
- Does BYO-KMS for a sub-collection of logs require HSM changes or infra-level key routing?
- Any immediate compliance red flags (auditability, segregation of duties) that would block a pilot?

Proposed owners: Hannah (security) to own compliance checklist; Marcus (infra) to validate KMS routing; Karthik (legal/product) to draft customer-facing exception and sign-off process. Lauren, can you coordinate CS/Sales communications if we proceed?

I'll assemble a short mutual action plan once we have confirmations.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Program Manager, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

--

Date: 2027-10-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-team: retention scope and BYO-KMS check-in

Monica — thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick thoughts:
- Scoped retention exceptions are doable at a dataset/route level, but we need to confirm whether 'ingest-debug' is already aggregated with other audit logs in the pipeline. If it's mixed, separation will require a short dev effort (~1-2 sprints) or a runtime tagging rule.
- BYO-KMS for a subset is trickier: we can route a subset of keys if the runtime honors key identifiers, but we need to validate that our caching layer won't store tokenized artifacts encrypted under the wrong key. That could cause recovery/rotation issues.
- Auditability: we'll need preserved provenance (who rotated, when) and immutable rotation logs. If Acme wants a 48-hour rotation window, that increases rotation churn and we must ensure we can surface those events to auditors (we have endpoints, but may need to extend retention of rotation logs).

I'll block time with Marcus later today to go over the pipeline map and with Legal Ops (cc'd) to understand the exact audit expectations.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, SRE Team <ops@acme.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-team: retention scope and BYO-KMS check-in

Thanks for the heads up. I pulled the pipeline diagrams and the kms_diagram.png attached. Initial engineering notes:
- If 'ingest-debug' is emitted on a separate Kafka topic we can apply different retention TTLs at storage tier without modifying the global retention service. If it's the same topic, we'll need a tagging + router change (estimate 3-5 days of dev + 2 days of QA).
- BYO-KMS: we can accept a customer-provided key identifier and route encryption calls to the customer's key for that topic, but two caveats: 1) our runtime must never cache decrypted payloads under the customer key if those payloads are later consumed alongside other keys; 2) key rotation support during a 48-hour window will require us to extend rotation event retention (Hannah mentioned this). Also need to confirm our HSM provider supports cross-tenant key import for the requested key type.
- Operational impact: slightly higher tail latency (~5-10ms) on writes when touching external KMS; should be fine for the pilot but we should throttle concurrency for that topic to avoid burst costs.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Hannah and I to validate topic separation by EOD tomorrow.
2) Karthik to draft an exception template that lists timebound constraints and audit deliverables.
3) If separation requires dev work, propose a short pilot using an isolated ingestion path so we don't change global retention behavior.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cross-team: retention scope and BYO-KMS check-in

Dropping in from the legal/product angle. Useful framing: if this is a short pilot solely for Acme support and the dataset is narrow, we can treat it as a timebound exception with customer-signed acknowledgment of residual risk. To proceed we'll need:
- A proposed exception duration (I suggest 60–90 days max for pilot)
- Clear owner for generating and preserving rotation proof (Hannah to confirm log retention)
- A defined rollback plan and a statement that the exception won't create operator-level access changes elsewhere.

I've attached an exception_template.docx (boilerplate) and drafted a short clause to add to the customer agreement covering ephemeral BYO keys for limited datasets. Also linking HubSpot: HBSP-49275 where Acme's request lives.

If everyone is aligned, Legal Ops can fast-track sign-off provided security validates the auditability story.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-10-06T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-team: retention scope and BYO-KMS check-in

Thanks team — quick consolidation and next steps. After reviewing engineering constraints and legal guidance, proposal below:

Decision: proceed with a scoped, timebound exception for the 'ingest-debug' category limited to 60 days, with the following guardrails:
- Isolation: Pilot will use an isolated ingestion path (no changes to global retention) to minimize blast radius. (Marcus to own implementation.)
- BYO-KMS: Accept customer key identifiers for the isolated path only. Rotation window constrained to 48 hours for the pilot; rotation events will be exported and retained for 365 days for audit purposes. (Hannah to own audit export validation.)
- Legal: Acme must sign the exception_template.docx acknowledging risks and agreeing to the 60-day window. (Karthik/Legal Ops to manage sign-off.)
- Communication: Lauren to prepare a one-page customer-facing summary and CS playbook in case of questions.

Owners and target dates:
- Marcus: confirm isolated path feasibility and prototype by 2027-10-11.
- Hannah: confirm rotation-event export and retention by 2027-10-11.
- Karthik/Legal Ops: send exception doc to Acme and request signature by 2027-10-08.
- Lauren: draft CS summary by 2027-10-08.

Sara (Acme) — please confirm that a 60-day pilot and the requirement to sign the exception doc works for you. Once we have sign-off we'll kick off a short M.A.P. and schedule a technical sync.

I'll open a short internal tracker and include links to the artifacts (drive + HubSpot). Thanks again for quick responses.

Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Program Manager, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
